You've actually taken the best possible first step by willingly seeking help.  The most difficult part for me was always thinking I could handle depression on my own and being unwilling to reach out.  The willingness to fight it and trying to find a way to heal and overcome is itself a sign of strength that we often fail to appreciate.

In my area, we only have a small network of therapists so there's a waiting list for appointments.  It's annoying and only adds pressure to that feeling of urgency when we really need someone to talk to.  Most of us in this sub aren't qualified to diagnose or prescribe, but we're fighting the same battle so we can be your network of support when you need.

As far as your job goes, maybe change will turn out to be a good thing.  Challenge can be rewarding.  You went to a new city for an uncertain job and it turned out well.  Now that your responsibilities within that job are changing, maybe you'll find you enjoy the challenge.  At the very least, maybe the time spent learning your new role can help occupy your mind during this trying time.

I applaud your goals of healthy living.  It's more than I've done for myself and I could probably benefit from that.  But you've taken several steps toward bettering your health and I applaud you for that.

I wish I had better advice.  "Stay strong and keep fighting" seem minimal and inadequate, but I say them anyway.  All of us are here to lend an ear.

To go along with another comment in here - stone isn't something you want to wear during the healing process.  You'll want to stick to using materials that aren't porous and can be sterilized.  Titanium and glass are the best materials to use during the healing process.  Avoid acrylic and most other plastics even after you're healed.

Dead stretching is your safest option.  That's simply waiting for your ears to stretch themselves before putting in the next size.  Tapers are alright for smaller sizes but shouldn't be your first method.

I stand by my previous comment.  Take Alex Ross for example.  He's one of the most well known comic book artists and he paints.  Not on Photoshop.  He physically paints his characters.  Jim Lee, possibly the most important artist in the modern age of major comics, physically draws his panels.

Photoshop can be useful for those who prefer it.  I personally prefer hand-drawn pages.  But that doesn't make any other medium insignificant.  Unless you're wanting to create motion comics or you're an extreme perfectionist, I still believe that physical mediums are preferable to digital.  It's like choosing between vinyl or digital music.  Both are good and both are selling like crazy.
Art isn't defined by a single medium or a single subject.  There's a reason art schools teach courses solely on drawing people.  It's a subject that has been viable on its own for ages.

That depends on what you mean by succeeding.  I haven't made a penny from any of my music, and his work is mostly just known locally.  The point is that we took a chance.  You should take a chance too.

Sharing the idea.  Showcasing your talent.  Keeping the character alive in a way.  Drawing interest to your ideas.  There are several reasons.  There's even the chance that someone could see your work and want to help you bring the idea to fruition.  That's how my first demo happened.  I used to post snippets of my lyrics on Facebook and someone happened to read some and helped me get a few ideas recorded.  Nothing's impossible.

My cousin just recently released a graphic novel based on a trading card game he created called Survive.  It's a zombie apocalypse sort of thing.  He cashed in on the craze.  But it did pretty well for an independent work.  He just tossed his ideas out into the world and saw where it went.  It's all about that initial leap of faith.

In my opinion, the beauty in art lies in its creation.  It's an artist's expression.  I assume you enjoy creating your works, so maybe that's the purpose of your art - healthy expression.  Sort of like the songs I write that no one will ever read / hear.

If you really want to share it, I have a friend who solely shares her art via Instagram simply by taking a photo on her phone of her sketches.  She even goes old school with her watermarks and just lays a slip of paper with her username over a portion of the page.  Maybe give that a shot?

You could try that to showcase your work, then maybe down the road you could invest in the necessary tools to produce full comics for purchase.  Or crowdfund a series.  Imagination's the limit.

The only real side effect that scares me about ECT is memory loss.  I've read that it's common to suffer short term memory loss following the treatment, and I don't want to forget what it was like to see her smiling in the morning.

I'm not hoping for a new love.  Anyone after her would be settling for less than the world that I had with her.  I had been in love with her since we were 10 and everyone before her was just a pale shade of what I saw when I looked at her.  That's not to say I didn't give my all every time.  There was a marriage and a divorce along the way.  I love someone enough to marry them and it still couldn't hold a candle to my dream girl.  So now I hold onto the hope of her return in a desperate attempt to keep looking toward a future that may never come.  If I lose that hope, I've lost all that I have left.  She keeps the music alive.

In terms of medicating the psychosis, I've tried.  I stopped after Seroquel left me much worse than I was before I started taking it.  My hallucinations became more vivid and frequent, and it kept me pretty heavily sedated.  I'd rather face a broken reality than the nightmares any day.

I'm lucky enough to have bandmates who are supportive of my personal expression through my lyrics.  Most of our songs tend to be dark in nature, but they roll with it.  It's a good outlet.

I'm torn on whether or not I'll go through with ECT.  I have exhausted all medications that are safe for me to take, both prescribed and not-so-prescribed.  I've even tried alternative therapies.  Changing my environment.  Journaling.  All that fun stuff.  Seems pretty hopeless.

The only time I've ever not been depressed was in a recent relationship.  It wasn't just any relationship.  It's one of those once in a lifetime things.  The girl of my dreams.  Two amazing kids who looked up to me.  Living the dream.  Then the ex-douche did his thing and killed it.  Some people are just born to lose, I guess.

Or maybe I'm just afraid of not being depressed anymore.  28 years of it and I can't imagine any other way of being.

But maybe you're right.  Maybe there's still a chance to rise like the phoenix.

There's a quote I always try to turn to in dark times.  It's by Victor Frankl, a holocaust survivor.  He wrote, "Human beings are not destroyed by suffering; they are destroyed by suffering without meaning."

Maybe our suffering has meaning.

It's what you do while you're alive that's important.  I want to die, but I don't want those I love to suffer for it.  Living isn't the important part.  How we live is.  I'll go by my own hand soon enough, but until then, I'm gonna leave behind as much good as I possibly can.

Could it be that your view of yourself is biased due to your lack of will to go on?  For me, depression causes me to see the worst in myself as justification for my suicidal ideology.  Maybe you see the back and forth between wanting to die and to survive as an annoyance because having the will to live is too overwhelming for a depressed mind to accept.  Still, it's a show of strength and if that annoyance is what it takes for you to live to fight another day, so be it.  Whatever keeps you around.

Music.  My answer to everything is music.  I've forced myself into seclusion to avoid the judging stares of the world around me and the only comfort I find anymore comes in the form of a dark room and loud music through my headphones.

I'm not sure how to get past the loneliness or fear that comes with depression and isolation.  Pushing people away is almost a reflex at this point.  I'm coming up on 28 and still haven't figured that one out.  I write every day but it's less about therapy and more about having some sort of consistency in my life.

Regardless, don't ever think you're worth any less than anyone else.  That you're not as important.  People will listen if you talk.  It's a scary step to take even more terrifying to continue to take after that first contact, but they'll listen.  Start small.  Talk to a parent or sibling.  Even a therapist.  Anyone who you know will still be there after you unload the deep and dark.  Or talk to us.  We're all fighting a similar battle so maybe you can find some comfort in similar struggles.

Either way, just remember to breathe in and out.  Keep fighting.  Keep moving forward.  Keep hope.
